fields.spec_version: JEDEC JESD238 — High Bandwidth Memory (HBM3) DRAM Standard (officially announced January 27, 2022)

spec_lineage_hbm.summary: First HBM; 1.0 Gb/s/pin; 1024-bit; up to 4 GB/stack; ~128 GB/s.
HBM2; 8 channels of 128 bits; up to 8 GB/stack; ~256-307 GB/s.
Up to 3.2-3.6 Gb/s/pin; up to 307 GB/s/stack; 12-Hi for 24 GB.
16 channels of 64 bits (1024-bit total); up to 6.4 Gb/s/pin; up to 819 GB/s/stack; 8-Hi (16 GB) / 12-Hi (24 GB) of 16 Gb dies; on-die + link ECC; RFM; RAS.
2048-bit interface; up to 8 Gb/s/pin; up to 2 TB/s; backwards compatible with HBM3 controllers.

key_changes_vs_hbm2e.impact: Finer access granularity; total still 1024 data pins.

key_changes_vs_hbm2e.change: Per-pin rate doubled to 6.4 Gb/s/pin (vs JEDEC HBM2E 3.2)
key_changes_vs_hbm2e.impact: Up to 819 GB/s per stack vs ~307.
Independent column streams per channel half.

key_changes_vs_hbm2e.change: 12-Hi stacks of 16 Gb dies (~30 µm thick) for 24 GB

backward_compat_traps.rule: HBM3 uses 16 channels of 64 bits where HBM2/HBM2E used 8 channels of 128 bits; total is still 1024 data pins.
backward_compat_traps.trap: A controller assuming HBM2's 8x128 map will mis-address an HBM3 stack even though pin count matches.

backward_compat_traps.rule: The 16 channels are independent and not necessarily synchronous; each has its own clock and command/address bus.
backward_compat_traps.trap: A controller assuming a single shared clock / lockstep will fail; each channel must be trained and scheduled independently.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Each 64-bit channel splits into two independent 32-bit pseudo-channels.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Treating a channel as monolithic 64-bit foregoes the independent column streams and reduces efficiency.

backward_compat_traps.rule: HBM3 mandates Refresh-Management (RFM) under high activate rates.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Omitting RFM can cause row-hammer-class corruption at sustained high throughput.

backward_compat_traps.rule: HBM3 adds on-die ECC, link ECC, CA parity, and alert/error reporting.
backward_compat_traps.trap: A controller ignoring the RAS alert path will miss uncorrectable errors and repair opportunities.

backward_compat_traps.rule: HBM4 (JESD270-4) widens the interface to 2048 bits; backwards compatible with HBM3 controllers but a different standard.
backward_compat_traps.trap: HBM3 and HBM4 are not the same width; do not size an HBM3 PHY for HBM4's 2048-bit interface.

fields.version_naming_history_note: HBM is standardized by JEDEC: Wide I/O (JESD229, 2011) -> HBM (JESD235, 2013) -> HBM2 (JESD235a, 2016) -> HBM2E (2018-2019) -> HBM3 (JESD238, announced January 27, 2022) -> HBM4 (JESD270-4, April 2025). HBM3 was the first to double the channel count to 16 x 64-bit while keeping the 1024-bit total width and to reach 6.4 Gb/s/pin / 819 GB/s per stack. SK Hynix produced the industry-first HBM3 used with NVIDIA's H100; its first-generation HBM3 chips were square.
